comment: The 20 itinerary themes. The build script spreads these across the hotels marked consider:true in hotel-options.json (e.g. 4 hotels x 5 themes, 5 x 4, 2 x 10, 1 x 20) so every generated plan is a unique hotel x theme combination. Placeholders: {hotel}, {area}, {station}, {walk}.

themes.title: Classic First-Timer Highlights
themes.pace: Moderate–full days
themes.blurb: The greatest-hits Seoul loop: palaces, a market day, N Seoul Tower, and a hanok evening — all routed so you return to {hotel} at night without wasted transfers.
themes.bestFor: You two, first time in Seoul — want the greatest hits without rushing, with time to linger together.

days.title: Palace core & old city
days.morning: Gyeongbokgung Palace (Royal Guard Changing Ceremony, usually 10:00/14:00 — verify) with free entry if wearing rented hanbok; National Folk Museum on the grounds if the weather turns.
days.afternoon: Bukchon Hanok Village viewpoint walk (arrive before 10:00 for calm streets, residents ask for quiet) then lunch in Insadong.
days.evening: Ikseon-dong hanok alley dinner and dessert; back to {hotel} on Line 3/1.

days.title: Markets & the tower
days.morning: Gwangjang Market brunch — bindaetteok (mung-bean pancake), mayak gimbap, yukhoe.
days.afternoon: Cheonggyecheon Stream stroll to Dongdaemun Design Plaza (DDP), then back past City Hall.
days.evening: Namsan Cable Car + N Seoul Tower at sunset (book the cable car slot in advance); late supper near {hotel}.

days.title: Change of pace — river or shopping
days.morning: Option A: Han River bike/ferry morning. Option B: Myeongdong shopping + Olive Young first pass.
days.afternoon: Lunch near {area}, then a second neighborhood — Seongsu for cafes and pop-ups or Hongdae for street energy.
days.evening: DDP Dream in Light free light show (nightly) or a show like JUMP/CHEF (non-verbal, zero Korean needed).

extraNights: Changdeokgung Huwon (Secret Garden) — book the guided slot in advance; autumn peak.
Jongmyo Shrine + Seochon village tea-house afternoon.
Lotte World Tower (Seoul Sky observatory) or COEX Aquarium if you want a big 'wow' day.
Free Seoul Walking Tour (reserve via english.visitseoul.net).
themes.planB: Rainy: swap outdoor palace time for National Palace Museum / National Folk Museum (both free, inside Gyeongbokgung) and the DDP museum.
themes.coupleVibe: You two, first time in Seoul — want the greatest hits without rushing, with time to linger together.

themes.title: Market & Street-Food Crawl
themes.pace: Grazing pace — meals are the anchors
themes.blurb: A eat-your-way-across-Seoul plan built around the markets and food alleys, with {hotel} as the evening reset point. Most meals are under ~₩12,000.
themes.bestFor: You two love to eat together — markets and street-food alleys at a grazing, hand-in-hand pace.

days.title: Gwangjang & Dongdaemun
days.morning: Gwangjang Market brunch: bindaetteok, mayak gimbap, yukhoe, mung-bean pancakes.
days.afternoon: Walk the Cheonggyecheon to Dongdaemun — grilled fish street (saengseon-gui alley) and the toy/stationery wholesale market for snacks and souvenirs.
days.evening: Jangchung-dong jokbal (glazed pork trotter) alley — a local institution; late tteokbokki near {hotel}.

days.title: Insadong, Tongin & Ikseon
days.morning: Tongin Market Dosirak Cafe — swap ₩5,000–10,000 for brass coins, fill a lunchbox tray (Tue–Sun 11:00–16:00; closed Mon).
days.afternoon: Insadong tea street + ssamziegil arcade snacks.
days.evening: Ikseon-dong hanok alleys: craft beer, soufflé pancakes, and small-plate Korean (jeon, japchae).

days.title: Myeongdong & late-night eats
days.morning: Slow start: {area} breakfast — gyeran-ppang, hotteok, and a proper coffee.
days.afternoon: Myeongdong street-food crawl (tornado potato, cheese corn dogs, egg bread) + a Korean-Chinese lunch (jajangmyeon/tangsuyuk) at a local favorite.
days.evening: AYCE BBQ night (Korean BBQ all-you-can-eat, ~₩20–35k) near {hotel}, then pojangmacha-style street snack on the way back.

extraNights: Mangwon Market + Seoul Battleship Park riverside walk.
Noryangjin Fish Market for a raw-fish (hoetjip) lunch — choose your fish upstairs.
Seongsu-dong cafe-and-bakery crawl (vegan/brunch spots included).
Hongdae food street after dark — tteokbokki, sundae, and street performers.
themes.planB: Rainy: swap market mornings for an indoor food hall (The Hyundai Seoul food court, Starfield COEX) — same grazing, dry feet.
themes.coupleVibe: You two love to eat together — markets and street-food alleys at a grazing, hand-in-hand pace.

themes.title: Cafe & Dessert Hop
themes.pace: Cafe-paced — sit, sip, stroll
themes.blurb: Three neighborhoods a day, two or three cafes each, one great lunch — a photo-worthy, low-exertion plan that always ends within an easy ride of {hotel}.
themes.bestFor: For two cafe lovers — slow mornings, beautiful spaces, dessert second-dates in every neighborhood.

days.title: Ikseon-dong & Insadong
days.morning: Hanok-roofed cafes in Ikseon-dong (soufflé pancakes, traditional teas) before the crowds.
days.afternoon: Insadong tea houses + ssamziegil craft floors; lunch at a jeon (savory pancake) house.
days.evening: Dessert bar hop in Jongno — bingsu/tiramisu modern takes; back to {hotel} by Line 3/1.

days.title: Seongsu & Euljiro
days.morning: Seongsu-dong 'Brooklyn of Seoul': warehouse bakeries, specialty roasters (open ~10:00–11:00).
days.afternoon: Lunch at a Seongsu brunch/burger spot, then Euljiro printing-alley cafes and nogari beer alleys.
days.evening: Euljiro neon at dusk + one more rooftop cafe; DDP Dream in Light on the way back.

days.title: Hongdae & Yeonnam
days.morning: Yeonnam-dong craft bakeries and roastery alleys (slow open — plan 11:00+).
days.afternoon: Hongdae style street + free market (Sat), then a themed cafe (animal/cat cafes optional).
days.evening: Han River picnic dessert stop (Gyeongui Line Forest Park) then back to {hotel}.

extraNights: Hannam-dong / Itaewon design-row coffee walk.
Cheongdam-dong dessert flagship stores (late opens, 12:00+).
Traditional tea ritual at a hanok tea house near Anguk.
Night bakery tour in Mapo — late-open specialty bakes.
themes.planB: Energy dip: skip the third neighborhood and camp at one great cafe with a view — the day still delivers.
themes.coupleVibe: For two cafe lovers — slow mornings, beautiful spaces, dessert second-dates in every neighborhood.

themes.title: Palaces & Heritage Walk
themes.pace: Steady — one palace per morning, tea in the afternoons
themes.blurb: The old-city Seoul of palaces, shrines, and hanok — most of it walkable from a Jongno/Insadong base and a short Line 3/1/4 ride from {hotel}.
themes.bestFor: You two want classic Seoul history together — palaces by morning, tea houses by afternoon.

days.title: Gyeongbokgung & Seochon
days.morning: Gyeongbokgung (guard changing ceremony; hanbok = free entry), National Palace Museum.
days.afternoon: Seochon village lunch + cafes (the quieter west side of the palace).
days.evening: Cheong Wa Dae (Blue House) grounds walk if open, or Gwanghwamun Square + King Sejong Story Museum (free).

days.title: Changdeokgung & Jongmyo
days.morning: Changdeokgung + Huwon Secret Garden (reserve the guided slot; autumn peak), Changgyeonggung greenhouse next door.
days.afternoon: Jongmyo Shrine (UNESCO, quiet) — guided tour times are limited, check on arrival.
days.evening: Unhyeongung + Ikseon-dong hanok dinner; Changgyeonggung 'Mulbit Yeonhwa' night media art through Nov 8.

days.title: Deoksugung, Namdaemun & the walls
days.morning: Deoksugung Palace + Jeongdong stonewall walkway + Jeongdong Theater traditional performance.
days.afternoon: Namdaemun Market (hanbok, crafts, knife-shopping alley) + Sungnyemun gate.
days.evening: Namsangol Hanok Village (free, folk games, tea) then Namsan cable car sunset if energy allows.

extraNights: Gyeonghuigung Palace + Seoul Museum of History (free).
Seoul City Wall walk: Naksan → Hyehwa section at golden hour.
Eunpyeong Hanok Village (calmer, newer) + Jingwansa temple lunch.
Museum Kimchikan kimchi-making class (Insadong, Tue–Sun).
themes.planB: Rainy: palace courtyards swap for museum interiors — National Museum of Korean Contemporary History (free, rooftop panorama) and the craft museum SeMoCA.
themes.coupleVibe: You two want classic Seoul history together — palaces by morning, tea houses by afternoon.

themes.title: Shopping & Beauty Haul
themes.pace: Market-paced — shop, compare, pack
themes.blurb: A shopping plan tuned for a serious haul: duty-free comparisons, Olive Young strategy, tax refunds, and luggage-friendly returns to {hotel}.
themes.bestFor: You two want to shop smart together — beauty, souvenirs, and gift hunting with easy hotel drop-offs.

days.title: Myeongdong beauty core
days.morning: Olive Young flagship + tester tour (no-buy pass first, decide later), Lohb's & CHICOR for higher-end lines.
days.afternoon: Myeongdong street stalls (socks, phone cases, cosmetics) + Daiso for packing supplies and gifts.
days.evening: Duty-free comparison at Lotte Duty Free (Myeongdong) — note prices, buy only what's clearly cheaper; N Seoul Tower night view.

days.title: Dongdaemun & underground malls
days.morning: Dongdaemun Design Plaza + underground shopping (fashion wholesale: note the 2-piece-minimum rule at Doota/Good Morning City).
days.afternoon: Cheonggyecheon walk + Euljiro stationery/paper shops (record stores too).
days.evening: Euljiro craft beer or Dongdaemun night market for accessories.

days.title: Hanbok, markets & tax refunds
days.morning: Namdaemun Market: hanbok, kitchen goods, souvenirs — bargaining is normal.
days.afternoon: Insadong crafts (brass, pottery, tea sets) + ssamziegil.
days.evening: Pack-and-sort night: organize receipts for the instant tax refund (keep purchases in original bags), then a farewell BBQ dinner.

extraNights: Gangnam underground shopping center + Starfield COEX (Starfield Library, K-pop merch).
Hyundai Seoul (Yeouido) — the current mega-mall experience with a rooftop garden.
Ewha fashion street + boutique alleys near Ewha Womans University.
Garak Market for wholesale fruit/gifts to take home.
themes.planB: Rainy: underground malls and department stores (Lotte Young Plaza, Hyundai) keep the haul going dry.
themes.coupleVibe: You two want to shop smart together — beauty, souvenirs, and gift hunting with easy hotel drop-offs.

themes.title: Nightlife & Late-Night Eats
themes.pace: Late shift — slow mornings, late nights
themes.blurb: Seoul after dark: neon alleys, pojangmacha tents, noraebang, live stages, and 24-hour supper — with {hotel} close to the last train home.
themes.bestFor: You two want Seoul after dark — neon alleys, a show, late-night eats, cozy walk home together.

days.title: Euljiro & Jongno after dark
days.afternoon: Late brunch, then Euljiro 'Hipjiro' printing alleys by daylight to scout the bars.
days.evening: Nogari beer + grilled pollack alley crawl; hop between Euljiro 3-ga craft bars; noraebang (singing room) session.
days.night: 24-hour soup or ramyeon near {hotel} — the classic Seoul 2 AM meal.

days.title: Hongdae streets & clubs
days.afternoon: Slow start, Hongdae street food + busking around 18:00–20:00.
days.evening: Live music bars (check post-rock/indie listings), then Hongdae club row or a late pojangmacha tent.
days.night: Last Line 2 train toward {area}, or 24-hour gopchang/samgyeopsal near the hotel.

days.title: Shows, DDP & night markets
days.afternoon: Afternoon show: JUMP martial-arts comedy or CHEF (Bibap) — both non-verbal, daily.
days.evening: DDP Dream in Light (free, nightly) + Dongdaemun night market.
days.night: Late-night fried chicken (chimaek) delivery to the hotel — the true Korean ritual.

extraNights: Itaewon/Hannam global bar street (wider world-cuisine night).
Gyeongui Line Forest Park late-night food trucks (Fri–Sat).
Changgyeonggung 'Mulbit Yeonhwa' palace night light art (through Nov 8).
Jamsil night: Lotte World Tower observatory after dark + Seokchon Lake lights.
themes.planB: Jet-lag early night: pivot to a 20:00 dinner + DDP lights + convenience-store dessert — still a Seoul night.
themes.coupleVibe: You two want Seoul after dark — neon alleys, a show, late-night eats, cozy walk home together.

themes.title: Museums & Galleries
themes.pace: Museum-paced — one ticketed anchor per day
themes.blurb: A dry-weather-proof plan across Seoul's best museums, galleries, and exhibition spaces — most anchors free or cheap, all within 30–40 min of {hotel}.
themes.bestFor: You two enjoy museums at your own pace — one thoughtful exhibition a day, no crowds to battle.

days.title: Gwanghwamun museum row
days.morning: National Museum of Korean Contemporary History (free; rooftop panorama of Gwanghwamun & Gyeongbokgung).
days.afternoon: Gyeongbokgung grounds + National Folk Museum (free) or National Palace Museum (free).
days.evening: Seoul Museum of Craft Art (SeMoCA, free) near Anguk, then Insadong dinner.

days.title: Yongsan & Itaewon
days.morning: National Museum of Korea (free, huge — pick 2–3 halls; English audio guides).
days.afternoon: Yongsan area lunch, then Leeum Museum of Art (book in advance) or D Museum.
days.evening: Itaewon international dinner + Hannam-dong gallery stroll.

days.title: DDP, Euljiro & a show
days.morning: DDP Design Museum + exhibition halls (check current shows); Dongdaemun History Hall (free).
days.afternoon: Euljiro indie galleries + K-Auction previews if open.
days.evening: Arario Museum in SPACE (Jongno) evening visit, or a musical/performance — check nol.world for listings.

extraNights: BANKSY: Still Here at The Hyundai Seoul (Yeouido) — CONFIRMED through Nov 3; prebook.
Seoul Museum of History (free, giant city model).
Hyundai Seoul ALT.1 + K-Auction preview circuit.
National Gugak Center Saturday traditional performance (₩10–20k).
themes.planB: Gallery fatigue: one long lunch at a museum cafe (NMK and Leeum both have great ones) and a river walk to reset.
themes.coupleVibe: You two enjoy museums at your own pace — one thoughtful exhibition a day, no crowds to battle.

themes.title: Han River & Parks
themes.pace: Outdoorsy but gentle — one park anchor per day
themes.blurb: Seoul's green-and-blue side: Han River parks, bikes, ferries, picnic culture, and a hill view — most of it free.
themes.bestFor: You two want fresh air together — Han River picnics, sunset views, gentle bike rides.

days.title: Yeouido river day
days.morning: Yeouido Hangang Park: bike along the river (Ttareungyi rentals ~₩3k/hr), riverside cafes.
days.afternoon: The Hyundai Seoul for lunch + BANKSY exhibition if still running (through Nov 3), rooftop garden.
days.evening: Banpo Hangang Park Moonlight Rainbow Fountain (check seasonal schedule) — picnic dinner on the lawn.

days.title: Ttukseom & Seoul Forest
days.morning: Ttukseom Hangang Park + Seoul Forest Park (deer, butterfly garden; free).
days.afternoon: Seongsu-dong lunch and cafes (right across the bridge).
days.evening: Eland Han River cruise (Yeouido dock) sunset departure — book ahead.

days.title: Haneul Park & the sky line
days.morning: Haneul Park silver-grass fields (seasonal peak in Nov) + 291 zigzag sky stairs — arrive early for the light.
days.afternoon: World Cup Park picnic or Mangwon Market lunch (nearby, local-feel).
days.evening: Han River History Tour riverside walk (runs through Nov 30) or Ichon reed-beds sunset.

extraNights: Gangseo Hangang Park eco-wetland bird-watching morning.
Gwangnaru bike track + reeds, then Amisa temple.
Dream Forest (Buk Seoul) + Wolyeongji pond autumn colors.
Eungbongsan night viewpoint for the Seoul skyline panorama.
themes.planB: Cold/rainy: swap to a jjimjilbang day (Aquafield/Dragon Hill) — spa warmth instead of park wind.
themes.coupleVibe: You two want fresh air together — Han River picnics, sunset views, gentle bike rides.

themes.title: Day-Trip Base Camp
themes.pace: Base-camp — big day out, calm day in
themes.blurb: Treats {hotel} as the base while you take the best day trips from Seoul: Suwon's fortress, the DMZ corridor, Nami Island, or temple mountains — then come home to the same bed.
themes.bestFor: You two want one easy day trip from Seoul and still sleep in the same bed that night.

days.title: Suwon Hwaseong
days.morning: ITX/Su-in line to Suwon (~30–45 min), Hwaseong Fortress walls + Hwaseong Haenggung palace.
days.afternoon: Suwon galbi lunch (the city's famous dish), then Jidong Market or the fortress cable car back.
days.evening: Return to {hotel}, late easy dinner in {area}.

days.title: DMZ / Imjingak (status-fluid)
days.morning: Tour pickup (book 2–4 weeks ahead; passport required) — Imjingak, the 3rd tunnel if open, Dorasan.
days.afternoon: Return by late afternoon; Paju outlet or Heyri art village stop if the tour allows.
days.evening: Rest night — convenience-store dinner + movie in the hotel room.

days.title: Nami Island & rail bikes
days.morning: ITX-Cheongchun to Gapyeong (~60–80 min); Nami Island ferry + ginkgo avenues (peak early Nov).
days.afternoon: Gangchon rail bike (book slot) or Garden of Morning Calm if open.
days.evening: Chuncheon dakgalbi (spicy stir-fried chicken) before the train home.

extraNights: Everland (book whole-day; Halloween 'Blood City' through early Nov if 2026 dates align).
Bukhansan National Park half-day hike (Baegundae summit, 2–3 hr up).
Incheon Chinatown + Wolmido seaside half-day.
Yongin Korean Folk Village — living-history day out.
themes.planB: Tour cancellation (DMZ status fluid): pivot to a Seoul fortress walk — Naksan city wall + DDP instead.
themes.coupleVibe: You two want one easy day trip from Seoul and still sleep in the same bed that night.

themes.title: K-Culture & Pop-Up Circuit
themes.pace: Late-ish — pop-ups, stages, and screen culture
themes.blurb: K-pop, K-drama, gaming, and pop culture: HiKR Ground, HYBE strolls, PC bangs, noraebang, and whatever pop-ups are running — with {hotel} as the transit hub.
themes.bestFor: You two are K-culture curious — pop-ups, music, and playful photo spots together.

days.title: HiKR Ground & Gwanghwamun
days.morning: HiKR Ground (K-Style Hub, free): K-pop MV photo stages + VR dance recording.
days.afternoon: Gwanghwamun + Cheonggyecheon; K-pop merch stores in Myeongdong (Music Korea, Ktown4u).
days.evening: K-pop TV show taping if a free audience slot lines up (check weekly listings).

days.title: HYBE, Yongsan & PC bangs
days.morning: HYBE headquarters + Dragon Hill walk (Yongsan) — mostly exterior/shop visit; check cafe hours.
days.afternoon: Yongsan I'Park Mall + e-sports PC bang session (cheap, fun, very Korean).
days.evening: Noraebang with song-request lists in English; late tteokbokki + corn dogs.

days.title: Pop-ups, Mnet & Jamsil
days.morning: Check pop-up listings near Seongsu/Hongdae (rotating; verify current week) — Seongsu is pop-up central.
days.afternoon: CJ ENM Center / Mnet studio exterior (Sangam) + DMC Star Plaza.
days.evening: Lotte World Tower night view or a K-musical — check nol.world for what's on.

extraNights: Gangnam K-Drama/Hallyu Star Avenue walk + JYP Soulcup cafe (Gangdong).
WILD WILD K-performance dance show (adult-leaning, Euljiro 3-ga).
LoL/e-sports watch party if a major tournament is live (check dates).
Idol-themed cafes and photocard hunting in Hongdae.
themes.planB: Pop-up closures: the HiKR Ground + PC bang + noraebang core still delivers a full K-culture day.
themes.coupleVibe: You two are K-culture curious — pop-ups, music, and playful photo spots together.

themes.title: Rainy-Day Indoor Plan
themes.pace: Weather-proof — indoors, connected by subway
themes.blurb: Seoul's weather insurance: a full indoor itinerary of malls, museums, spas, and food halls — each anchor reachable from {hotel} without stepping outside for more than a block.
themes.bestFor: You two want a weather-proof plan — malls, museums, and a warm jjimjilbang evening.

days.title: Mega-mall loop
days.morning: The Hyundai Seoul (Yeouido): food hall, rooftop garden under cover, BANKSY until Nov 3.
days.afternoon: IFC Mall underground dining + Starfield COEX (Starfield Library, aquarium, K-pop stores).
days.evening: Dinner at COEX food court or Gangnam underground mall; dry subway all the way home.

days.title: Museum & spa day
days.morning: National Museum of Korea (free, huge, all indoors).
days.afternoon: Lunch at NMK cafe, then Leeum Museum (book) or Yongsan I'Park mall.
days.evening: Dragon Hill / Aquafield jjimjilbang evening — scrub, sauna, sleep in a heated room.

days.title: DDP & Euljiro indoors
days.morning: DDP Design Museum + exhibition halls; Dongdaemun underground shopping.
days.afternoon: Lotte Young Plaza + Myeongdong underground shopping center (connected by subway passages).
days.evening: Korean-Japanese dinner (ramen) near {hotel} — Menten or a local favorite, then convenience-store dessert.

extraNights: Lotte World Adventure (mostly indoor) — Halloween decor through mid-Nov if 2026 dates align.
Arario Museum in SPACE (Jongno).
Gotomall (Express Bus Terminal underground mall) + Gangnam food hall.
Ewha ECC complex + Sinchon indoor shopping street.
themes.planB: The day IS the plan B — rainy-day itineraries just swap anchors if a venue closes.
themes.coupleVibe: You two want a weather-proof plan — malls, museums, and a warm jjimjilbang evening.

themes.title: Budget-Smart Seoul
themes.pace: Moderate — wallet-first, free first
themes.blurb: The full Seoul experience at the lowest sensible spend: free museums, hanbok-for-free-entry tricks, ₩ lunchboxes, street food over sit-down, and transit passes — all routed from {hotel}.
themes.bestFor: You two want it to feel rich without overspending — free gems, market meals, smart value.

days.title: Free old-city day
days.morning: Gyeongbokgung with rented hanbok (free palace entry), National Folk Museum (free).
days.afternoon: Tongin Market dosirak lunchbox (₩5–10k), then Seochon walk.
days.evening: Gwanghwamun Square + Cheonggyecheon lights (free); convenience-store dinner stash.

days.title: Market & museum day
days.morning: Gwangjang Market brunch (bindaetteok ~₩5–8k, mayak gimbap), free tastings while you shop.
days.afternoon: DDP + Dongdaemun History Hall (free), Euljiro window shopping.
days.evening: DDP Dream in Light (free) + street food dinner.

days.title: River & discount day
days.morning: Han River bike + picnic (convenience-store lunch on the lawn — the Korean way).
days.afternoon: Korea Sale FESTA window if running (recent pattern Nov 9–30) — price-compare duty-free vs. Olive Young sale stock.
days.evening: AYCE BBQ at a budget chain (~₩20k) or jjimjilbang overnight option (spa + sleep = free hotel night hack).

extraNights: Free Seoul Walking Tour (reserve).
Budget day-trip: Suwon fortress (cheap rail + ₩ entry) instead of DMZ.
Jeongdong Theater 'free preview' performances when available.
Lotte Mart last-day grocery run for gifts (instant tax refund ≥₩15,000).
themes.planB: Rainy budget day: National Museum (free) + COEX library (free) + cheap ramen lunch.
themes.coupleVibe: You two want it to feel rich without overspending — free gems, market meals, smart value.

themes.title: Photo & Golden-Hour Loop
themes.pace: Early starts — golden & blue hour anchors
themes.blurb: A photographer's Seoul: dawn light on the city wall, palace geometry at opening, neon at dusk, and night views — with efficient routes back to {hotel}.
themes.bestFor: You two love golden-hour photos together — palaces, river, and neon at blue hour.

days.title: Old city light
days.dawn: Naksan city wall sunrise walk (city wall + old-town rooftops).
days.day: Gyeongbokgung geometry at opening (arrive 09:00 before crowds; guard change at 10:00).
days.dusk: N Seoul Tower / Namsan cable car blue hour + night panorama.

days.title: Neon & design night
days.day: Seongsu-dong warehouse textures + Euljiro printing alleys (late open — plan 14:00+).
days.dusk: DDP curves at blue hour (design museum exterior + Dream in Light).
days.night: Dongdaemun night market neon; long-exposure practice.

days.title: River & sky
days.dawn: Haneul Park silver grass at first light (misty, seasonal peak).
days.day: Gangnam/Starfield Library shelves + COEX aquarium tunnel.
days.dusk: Banpo Moonlight Rainbow Fountain (seasonal) or Eland cruise at sunset.

extraNights: Eungbongsan night viewpoint.
Changdeokgung Huwon autumn foliage at opening light.
Cheonggyecheon lantern/night stream walk.
Gwangnaru reeds at golden hour.
themes.planB: Grey sky: pivot to interiors — SeMoCA craft museum, Hyundai Seoul ALT.1, Starfield Library — where light doesn't matter.
themes.coupleVibe: You two love golden-hour photos together — palaces, river, and neon at blue hour.

themes.title: Slow Mornings & Spa Recharge
themes.pace: Very gentle — one anchor per day, late starts
themes.blurb: The reset trip: late breakfasts, jjimjilbang sessions, tea houses, and unhurried neighborhoods — everything within an easy ride of {hotel}.
themes.bestFor: You two need to actually recharge — late starts, spas, tea houses, unhurried wandering.

days.title: Spa & tea day
days.morning: Sleep in; late brunch at a cafe near {hotel}.
days.afternoon: Jjimjilbang session (Aquafield or Dragon Hill — saunas, hot pools, snack corner).
days.evening: Hanok tea house in Insadong/Ikseon-dong; light dinner of jeon + makgeolli.

days.title: Seochon & the slow old city
days.morning: Late start, Seochon village cafes and bookshops.
days.afternoon: Gyeongbokgung at a stroll's pace (hanbok optional), National Folk Museum.
days.evening: Gwanghwamun Square walk + early dinner; early night.

days.title: River calm
days.morning: Han River park bench morning — coffee + book on the lawn.
days.afternoon: Ferry to Banpo (Han River bus) for a slow afternoon; Some Sevit floating islands.
days.evening: Picnic dinner on the riverbank or room-service-style takeout at {hotel}.

extraNights: Bukchon slow photo walk before 10:00.
Templestay night (Jogyesa area / Hwagyesa) — English programs bookable.
Haneul Park easy sunset (short walk from World Cup Stadium).
Massage/foot-spa session in Myeongdong's spa district.
themes.planB: Energy returns mid-day: add one spontaneous neighborhood — the itinerary is designed to flex.
themes.coupleVibe: You two need to actually recharge — late starts, spas, tea houses, unhurried wandering.

themes.title: Neighborhood Immersion
themes.pace: Moderate — one neighborhood per half-day, no backtracking
themes.blurb: Live Seoul like a local: one distinct neighborhood after another — markets, alley bars, campus streets, and village lanes — chained into loops that start and end near {hotel}.
themes.bestFor: You two want neighborhood texture — alleys, cafes, and local streets without backtracking.

days.title: Jongno to Euljiro loop
days.morning: Jongno 3-ga lunch market + tapgol park; wander the printing/paper alleys.
days.afternoon: Euljiro craft workshops and indie galleries.
days.evening: Euljiro nogari beer alleys + pajeon; night bus/walk back to {area}.

days.title: Mapo-Gongdeok loop
days.morning: Mapo meat alley + Gongdeok food street (beyond tourist maps).
days.afternoon: Gyeongui Line Forest Park / Yeontral Park walk to Hongdae.
days.evening: Hongdae free market (Sat), busking, indie stages.

days.title: Seongsu to Seoul Forest
days.morning: Seongsu-dong factories-turned-cafes and flagship pop-ups.
days.afternoon: Seoul Forest Park + Under Stand Avenue container shops.
days.evening: Sungsu evening restaurants (gopchang, pasta, wine bars) then home.

extraNights: Itaewon/Hannam global-village crawl.
Mangwon Market morning + Yeonnam-dong roasteries.
Changsin-dong market alleys + Ihwa mural village.
Sinchon/Ewha campus streets for young-Seoul energy.
themes.planB: Weather: pick the covered versions — underground mall neighborhoods (Gangnam, Express Bus Terminal) instead of alleys.
themes.coupleVibe: You two want neighborhood texture — alleys, cafes, and local streets without backtracking.

themes.title: Family & Kid-Friendly
themes.pace: Kid-paced — short walks, early dinners
themes.blurb: Seoul that works with kids: aquariums, amusement parks, hands-on museums, and early-friendly food — with {hotel}'s central location keeping meltdown-transit short.
themes.bestFor: You two want an easy, low-stress rhythm — gentle walks, early dinners, relaxed evenings together.

days.title: Lotte World & aquarium
days.morning: Lotte World Adventure (indoor rides — perfect for unpredictable weather) + Seokchon Lake walk.
days.afternoon: COEX Aquarium + Starfield Library (shelves wow kids, and it's free).
days.evening: Easy early dinner near the hotel; room wind-down.

days.title: Palace, hanbok & markets
days.morning: Gyeongbokgung in hanbok (free entry for the whole family; changing ceremony).
days.afternoon: Gwangjang Market snack tour — let the kids pick from stalls.
days.evening: Cheonggyecheon stream splash-and-stroll; DDP light show.

days.title: Animals & parks
days.morning: Seoul Grand Park zoo + Seoul Land (open-air, check weather) OR Seoul Forest deer park (free).
days.afternoon: Picnic lunch; Children's Museum at National Museum of Korea (hands-on, free-ish).
days.evening: Family jjimjilbang night — kids love the pools and snack bar.

extraNights: Everland full day (rides + safari; Halloween decor in season).
Trick Eye / Alive Museum photo museums (rainy-day gold).
Rail bike near Seoul (Gangchon) as an active day out.
Busan-style aquarium + Namsan cable car combo day.
themes.planB: Tired kids: cut the day at the first sign — every anchor has a 'we already won' version.
themes.coupleVibe: You two want an easy, low-stress rhythm — gentle walks, early dinners, relaxed evenings together.

themes.title: Romance & Date Night
themes.pace: Polished — golden hours and good tables
themes.blurb: Seoul for two: sunset views, a nice dinner, a night show or riverside walk — with {hotel} as the elegant home base that makes the evening effortless.
themes.bestFor: You two want a proper date — sunset tower, nice dinner, night walk, river cruise.

days.title: Tower & rooftop night
days.afternoon: Late afternoon cable car to N Seoul Tower; lock your padlock on the terrace.
days.evening: Tower dinner (book a window table) or return to {area} for a rooftop-bar dinner near {hotel}.
days.night: Night walk down Namsan's mountain path — quieter and prettier than the cable car.

days.title: Palace light & hanok dinner
days.afternoon: Gyeongbokgung at closing light (Sept–Nov hours end ~17:00, check), or Changgyeonggung 'Mulbit Yeonhwa' night art (through Nov 8).
days.evening: Ikseon-dong private-room Korean dinner; then a traditional tea nightcap.

days.title: River cruise night
days.afternoon: Slow day: Seongsu cafes + Seoul Forest.
days.evening: Eland Han River sunset cruise with wine (book ahead); dinner at a Yeouido riverside restaurant.
days.night: Banpo fountain show + night bus back to {hotel}.

extraNights: Private hanok tea ceremony (book via Insadong tea houses).
Musical night out — check nol.world for current shows.
WILD WILD K-performance (adult date-night, Euljiro).
Han River private picnic kit + Bluetooth speaker sunset.
themes.planB: Rain: swap the tower for COEX aquarium tunnel + Starfield Library + a nice indoor dinner — still cinematic.
themes.coupleVibe: You two want a proper date — sunset tower, nice dinner, night walk, river cruise.

themes.title: Fitness & Morning Runs
themes.pace: Active — run/hike/walk first, sightsee after
themes.blurb: A movement-first Seoul: riverside runs, a mountain morning, bike loops, and stretching breaks — with shower-and-refuel at {hotel} after each session.
themes.bestFor: You two want to move together — sunrise riverside stroll, easy hike, then big lunch.

days.title: Han River run
days.morning: Sunrise 5–10k along the Han River park nearest to {area} (flat, popular, safe; Ttareungyi bikes for warm-up).
days.day: Protein-heavy Korean lunch (samgyetang or grilled chicken), then a light museum afternoon.
days.evening: Stretch + spa evening (foot bath or jjimjilbang).

days.title: Bukhansan hike
days.morning: Bukhansan Baegundae summit trail (2–3 hr up, steep sections; start before 08:00, bring water) or the easier Dobongsan/Mangwolsa loop.
days.day: Big reward lunch (BBQ), then rest at the hotel.
days.evening: Easy night — movie or DDP walk.

days.title: City-wall stair day
days.morning: Naksan → Hyehwa city-wall stair section (great intervals) + Ihwa mural village detour.
days.day: Lunch in Daehakro, then Gyeongui Line Forest Park recovery stroll.
days.evening: Stretching class or quiet sushi/samgyeopsal dinner near {hotel}.

extraNights: Gwanaksan sunrise trail + Yeonjuam hermitage.
Inwangsan tiger-rock scramble + city wall.
Gangseo eco-wetland early-morning bird + bike loop.
Achasan fortress hill sunset run.
themes.planB: Injury/rest day: swap for a jjimjilbang 'active recovery' day — saunas and gentle pools count.
themes.coupleVibe: You two want to move together — sunrise riverside stroll, easy hike, then big lunch.

themes.title: Night Market & Food Marathon
themes.pace: Marathon — but it's eating, so it's fine
themes.blurb: A focused night-by-night food marathon across Seoul's evening-eating spots — from market stalls to late-night BBQ — with {hotel} always one easy line home.
themes.bestFor: You two want to eat your way through Seoul at night — market stalls to late BBQ, together.

days.title: Gwangjang night session
days.evening: Gwangjang Market after dark (stalls run late): yukhoe, bindaetteok, mayak gimbap, and makgeolli with the ajummas.
days.night: Walk off the first round along Cheonggyecheon to Dongdaemun; fried-chicken snack if still hungry.

days.title: Euljiro & Jongno circuit
days.evening: Euljiro 3-ga nogari (grilled pollack) + draft beer alleys; then Jongno 3-ga pajeon-and-makgeolli streets.
days.night: 24-hour gopchang or ramyeon near {hotel} as the closer.

days.title: Myeongdong & Hongdae finale
days.evening: Myeongdong street-food final pass (egg bread, tornado potato, cheese corn dogs) → Hongdae food street (tteokbokki, sundae, grilled skewers).
days.night: Cup-bap or late soup from a convenience store — the eternal Korean nightcap.

extraNights: Noryangjin Fish Market night session (raw fish + soju).
Dongdaemun grilled-fish street late run.
Mangwon Market evening (locals' market, quieter than Gwangjang).
Jangchung-dong jokbal night walk.
themes.planB: Full: skip dinner, go straight to dessert-and-tea night — there is always room for bingsu.
themes.coupleVibe: You two want to eat your way through Seoul at night — market stalls to late BBQ, together.

themes.title: Last-Day Convenience & Airport Flow
themes.pace: Easy — zero panic, zero missed flights
themes.blurb: The final Seoul block done right: last-minute shopping with easy tax refunds, a farewell dinner near {hotel}, and a timed airport transfer plan so departure is boring.
themes.bestFor: You two on your last nights — easy shopping, farewell dinner, smooth airport send-off.

days.title: Final shop & pack
days.morning: Last Olive Young / Daiso run near {area} — keep receipts for instant tax refund.
days.afternoon: Lunch at a favorite revisited spot; Lotte Mart grocery run for edible gifts (tax refund ≥₩15,000).
days.evening: Pack-and-sort night: receipts in one pouch, liquids in the bag, luggage scale check.

days.title: Farewell day
days.morning: One last easy anchor near {hotel} — a palace, market, or cafe you loved.
days.afternoon: Farewell Korean lunch (samgyeopsal or samgyetang); final walk of {area}.
days.evening: Transfer plan: AREX from Seoul Station (verify last-train time against your flight), airport limousine stop near {hotel}, or pre-booked taxi. Confirm 3 hours before departure at ICN.

extraNights: Buffer-day rule: keep one completely free day before departure.
Re-check the AREX timetable and your hotel's limousine stop the night before.
If leaving very early, book the airport limousine pick-up the evening prior.
Keep ₩50k–100k cash for the airport-side needs.
themes.planB: Traffic/weather delay: fall back to AREX (rail is weather-proof) and buffer 90 extra minutes.
themes.coupleVibe: You two on your last nights — easy shopping, farewell dinner, smooth airport send-off.
